content:
Since I expect that verifying a lot of the current formalisation claims (and those yet to come) on the Erdos problems site will be an initial rush, I wanted to clarify a couple of things:

1) My plan was to announce on the Erdos site that all proof claims (with an accompanied formalisation) should be run through Palomar, and that when checking the correctness of a proof claim I will inspect the statement of Palomar.
2) As a consequence, it would be nice if any claim for a solution to an Erdos problem counted as notable enough to Palomar. Do you have an idea whether this will be the case?
3) Does the Palomar team have any objection to me encouraging the use of Palomar in this way?

I'm giving a personal answer, not yet a "collective" answer, but 1) seems a great plan, and I would presume that 2) would be a "very obvious yes", and 3) I imagine this could only be a good thing (as it would help encourage others to follow your lead).
Yes, I'm fairly confident quoting an Erdos problem number will easily clear the notability bar. If you hear of any counterexamples we'll treat it as a bug report!

Now I'm wondering what's the least interesting possible resolution among the remaining Erdos problems... Are there any for which the resolution is plausibly, "False. Here's a counterexample, found by exhaustive brute force search"?
Plenty! E.g. 64 (which has been proved for all large n, but might be false for some small n for boring reasons).
